verses.text: Jesus also told his disciples, “A rich man had a manager, and someone reported that the manager was wasting his property.”
He called the manager in and said, ‘What’s this I hear about you? Give me the accounts. You can’t manage my property anymore.’
“The manager thought to himself, ‘What am I going to do? My boss is taking away my job. I’m not strong enough to dig, and I’m too embarrassed to beg.”
“‘I know what I’ll do. When I lose this job, people will welcome me into their homes.’”
“He called in each person who owed his boss money. He asked the first, ‘How much do you owe my boss?’”
“The man said, ‘A hundred measures of olive oil.’ The manager said, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and make it fifty.’”
“Then he asked another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ The manager told him, ‘Take your bill and write eighty.’”
“The master praised the dishonest manager for acting shrewdly. People of this age are more streetwise with their own kind than people who live in the light.”
“So I’m telling you: use worldly wealth to make friends, so that when it’s gone, you may be welcomed into eternal homes.”
“Whoever is trustworthy with very little is trustworthy with much. Whoever is dishonest with very little is dishonest with much too.”
“So if you haven’t been trustworthy with worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?”
“And if you haven’t been trustworthy with someone else’s property, who will give you property of your own?”
“No servant can serve two masters. They’ll hate one and love the other, or be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and money.”
The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and sneered at Jesus.
He said to them, “You make yourselves look righteous in front of people, but God knows your hearts. What people honor is detestable to God.”
“The Law and the Prophets were in effect until John. Since then, the good news of God’s Kingdom has been preached, and people are pressing their way into it.”
“Heaven and earth could pass away more easily than even the tiniest mark of the Law disappearing.”
“Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery. And anyone who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.”
“There was a rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and enjoyed luxury every day.”
“A poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores, was laid at the rich man’s gate.”
“He longed to eat the scraps falling from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.”
“The poor man died, and angels carried him to Abraham’s side. The rich man died too and was buried.”
“In Hades, suffering terribly, the rich man looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus beside him.”
“He called out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me! Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. I’m suffering in this fire!’”
“But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember: you had good things during your lifetime, while Lazarus had bad things. Now he’s comforted here, and you’re suffering.”
“‘Besides, a huge gulf has been fixed between us and you. Nobody can cross from here to you, or from there to us.’”
“The rich man said, ‘Then please, Father, send Lazarus to my father’s house—”
“‘I have five brothers. Let him warn them so they won’t end up in this place of torment too.’”
“Abraham answered, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’”
“The rich man said, ‘No, Father Abraham. But if someone comes to them from the dead, they’ll turn back to God.’”
“Abraham told him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, they won’t be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.’”
